svg.text: Everything between the buildings. The same two locked houses stand in every tile; only the public realm evolves. Each street answers a different question.
same camera · same building language · same scale · no people, life implied
Q · what does the street look like before we try?
flags · kerb · quiet tarmac · one lamp, one bin
grass verge · five limes · canopy over the walk
deep verges both sides · the road narrows to fit
Q · what if brick paving dominates?
pavers wall-to-wall · darker course for the carriageway
Q · what if seating becomes social?
three benches, a hedge backrest, a lamp to talk under
Q · what if flowers are the identity?
raised brick planters both sides · colour with a reason
Q · what if traffic almost disappears?
bollards close it · one surface · chalk and bicycles
Q · what if arrival defines the street?
shelter, flag, timetable, bench · the town’s front door
Q · what if crossing is the safest act?
zebra · two Belisha beacons · tightened kerbs
Q · what if the street pauses?
paving swells into a square · tree, two benches, pillar box
Q · what if Friday writes the street?
three striped stalls on the closed carriageway · evidence of life
Q · all of it, in measure
verge + trees + brick walk + zebra + planter + bench
narrow carriageway, always; kerbs low and rounded; one surface change means one message; furniture in the accent family; nothing wider than a conversation.
SHEET 03 MADE IT LOVABLE · SHEET 04 GIVES IT GROUND
no medieval lanes, no Dutch woonerf pastiche, no American widths — a modern English village street, 1978

LEAD’S VERDICT — strongest three: ST-02 THE AVENUE (trees give the town its ceiling; green is the one thing the buildings don’t supply) · ST-10 THE POCKET SQUARE (the pause is where the simulation gets a stage) · ST-07 THE PLAY STREET (near-zero traffic is ERA’s values made physical).

RECOMMENDED — ST-12 THE ERA STREET: verge and trees from 02, brick walking surface on a low rounded kerb, a narrow quiet carriageway, zebra and Belisha at crossings, a planter and a bench wherever the street pauses (10), bollards where it closes (07).

WHY IT BELONGS — the street supplies what the buildings withhold (green, and pattern on the ground), repeats their materials at ground pitch, and keeps colour in flowers and furniture: the street frames; the houses speak. Negative finding kept: ST-04’s all-brick ground swallows the brick buildings.
